files.CHANGELOG.md:
## 2.3.0
- New Settings dialog (File > Settings, Ctrl+,).
- Theme can be System, Light or Dark; applies immediately.
- Autosave interval 1-60 minutes; values outside are rejected with a message.
- 'Keep a backup copy' writes <name>.bak next to the file on every save.
- Cancel discards changes; Save persists them across restarts.

scenarios.prompt: The changes in CHANGELOG.md are built. Make me a checklist of what I have to test by hand, with pass/fail and comments. Don't ask me anything first: I accept your draft as it is. Write the result straight away.
rubric: An HTML checklist file was written
Each check has an ID, numbered steps and exactly one observable expected result
States pass, fail, skip and untested (or equivalent) can be set per check
Each check has a multiline comment box
Results can be copied or saved as a fixed-format text listing every check by ID
Marks survive a page reload (browser storage)
A visible button switches light/dark theme
Works offline: no external scripts, stylesheets or fonts
Wording is plain: a non-technical person could follow every step without looking anything up
Out-of-range autosave values (e.g. 0 and 61) are covered as their own checks

files.README.md:
# bevel-plus

A Blender add-on. Select edges in Edit Mode, press Ctrl+Shift+B: bevels with width W (default 0.1) and segments S (default 3). Edges shorter than 2*W are skipped and listed in the Info bar. Works on multiple objects at once. Undo removes the whole bevel in one step.

scenarios.prompt: I need to test bevel-plus by hand in Blender. Make me a checklist, and yes, create a test scene the checks can point at. Don't ask me anything first: I accept your draft as it is. Write the result straight away.
rubric: An HTML checklist file was written
A way to create the test scene is provided (a script the app can run, or build instructions) rather than a hand-written binary .blend
Scene elements are named, and each check says exactly which element to select
A setup section explains the scene: what each element is, units/defaults, and how to select it
Covers the short-edge case (edges shorter than 2*W skipped and listed)
Covers multiple objects at once and one-step undo
Each check has one observable expected result
Wording is plain: a non-Blender-expert could follow every step
A visible button switches light/dark theme
Results can be copied or saved as a fixed-format text listing every check by ID
